did_you_know.text: Did you know? In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD stirred his spirit to fulfill the word spoken through Jeremiah.
Did you know? Cyrus’s proclamation was circulated throughout his entire kingdom, both orally and in writing, rather than being merely a local announcement.
Did you know? Cyrus declared that the LORD, the God of heaven, had given him all the kingdoms of the earth, and that the LORD had commanded him to build a temple for Him in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Cyrus addressed everyone among the Israelites who was willing to go, calling them to return to Jerusalem and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel.
Did you know? Those who remained where they lived were instructed to support the returning exiles with silver, gold, goods, livestock, and voluntary offerings for the house of God in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Those who returned included the heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and Levites; the text emphasizes that God stirred their spirits to go up and build.
Did you know? The people living in the surrounding area also willingly helped the returning exiles with silver articles, gold, goods, livestock, and gifts.
Did you know? Cyrus brought out the articles from the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his own god.
Did you know? The temple articles were handed over by Mithredath the treasurer to Sheshbazzar, whom the text calls the governor of Judah.
Did you know? The text lists the types and numbers of the temple articles, including thirty gold basins, one thousand silver basins, and twenty-nine knives.
Did you know? In summary, the total number of gold and silver articles that Sheshbazzar brought up with the exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem was 5,400.
